bio: I study how people, politics, and technology shape one another. My research brings artificial intelligence, machine learning, network analysis, and natural language processing to social and political data, with an emphasis on interpretable methods for understanding behavior, narratives, and emotions. I also build research software and mentor student researchers.

writing.researchIntro: I use artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning, network analysis, and natural language processing to uncover patterns in social and political data.
researchNarrative: I am particularly interested in questions that are straightforward to pose but computationally difficult to answer. How do networks reveal political influence and polarization? What can images, video, and audio tell us about communication, social divisions, and the visibility of political power? I build original datasets and research tools to investigate these questions.

My projects connect computational methods with substantive social science questions. They examine how people stand near one another in public space, where political parties display their symbols, how judges participate in hearings, and how political actors communicate through speech and emotion. Across this work, I distinguish descriptive patterns from causal explanations and ask whether a measure captures the concept it claims to represent.

I also evaluate the systems doing the measuring. I compare computational judgments with human expertise, study biases in AI-generated representations, and develop interpretable measures and reproducible workflows. Open Python software and collaboration with student researchers are central to how I do this work.

researchThemes.name: Politics in public space
researchThemes.description: I study social distance, visible identities, flags, party offices, and the ways political power becomes visible in everyday surroundings.

researchThemes.name: Networks and political influence
researchThemes.description: I use network models to examine elite interactions, lobbying, information diffusion, and political polarization.

researchThemes.name: Communication and emotion
researchThemes.description: I combine images, video, speech, and text to investigate nonverbal behavior and political communication in news, diplomacy, debates, and court hearings.

researchThemes.name: AI measurement and bias
researchThemes.description: I test the accuracy, biases, and limitations of language and vision models, with attention to validation, interpretation, and reproducibility.

researchThemes.name: History and video games
researchThemes.description: I ask what it means for a game to get history right, examining how games reconstruct architecture and other dimensions of the past while simplifying or inventing others.

researchThemes.name: Research software
researchThemes.description: I develop Python tools that help researchers extract, label, and analyze social information from images, video, audio, and webpages.

writing.teachingIntro: I teach data science, machine learning, and computational social science, and supervise student research across these areas.
teachingNarrative: My courses combine lectures and concept quizzes with labs, projects, and Kaggle challenges. Students work with real datasets, implement methods, evaluate models, and explain their decisions. Teaching in small liberal arts classrooms, large lectures, and mixed in-person and remote settings has also led me to use flipped modules, structured peer review, and low-stakes assessments.
I supervise student research in computational social science and AI.

teachingPrinciples.title: Use the method
teachingPrinciples.description: I ask students to apply methods to messy, real-world problems through labs, projects, and individual and team challenges.

teachingPrinciples.title: Understand why it works
teachingPrinciples.description: Programming and AI tools support the work, while exams test the mathematical and conceptual understanding students need to judge the results.

teachingPrinciples.title: Make assumptions visible
teachingPrinciples.description: Classroom exercises turn questions about bias, evaluation, and the limits of AI into things students can inspect and discuss.

teachingPrinciples.title: Build relationships
teachingPrinciples.description: I meet students to discuss their goals, coursework, and next steps, and maintain contact after the semester ends.

teachingPrinciples.title: Make research accessible
teachingPrinciples.description: I supervise student projects in computational social science and AI.

writing.aboutIntro: My work spans empirical and methodological applications in computational social science, computer vision, generative AI, natural language processing, and video games. I focus on interpretable, scalable methods for measuring behavior, narratives, and emotions across platforms. I also build open-source research tools and mentor student researchers.
